# Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K

## Summary

Given an array and a window size `k`, find the largest sum of any `k`
consecutive elements. The window length is fixed — this is not "maximum
subarray of any length" (that is Kadane's).

## Constraints

- `1 <= k <= nums.length` in every test case; behaviour for `k > nums.length`
  is deliberately left undefined.
- Values may be negative, so the answer can be negative.
- The array is not sorted and is not modified.

## Examples

| Input | Output | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2], 3` | `9` | window `[5, 1, 3]` |
| `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 1` | `5` | `k = 1` degenerates to "the maximum element" |
| `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 5` | `15` | `k = n` is the whole array |
| `[-1, -2, -3, -4], 2` | `-3` | window `[-1, -2]`, the least bad pair |

## Edge Cases

- `k = 1` and `k = nums.length`, the two degenerate windows.
- All-negative arrays — initialising `maxSum` to `0` instead of the first
  window is the classic bug here.
- The best window sitting at the very start or very end, where an off-by-one in
  the loop bounds hides.
- Ties between two windows with the same sum.

## Complexity

- **Time:** `O(n)` — one pass to build the first window, then one add and one
  subtract per remaining element.
- **Space:** `O(1)`.
- Brute force for comparison: `O(n·k)`, recomputing each window from scratch.

## Why This Category

The defining move of a sliding window is reusing the previous window's work:
`windowSum += nums[i] - nums[i - k]`. Every element enters the window once and
leaves once. Reach for a fixed-size window whenever a question asks about "every
contiguous run of exactly k" — sums, averages, distinct counts, anagram matches.

## Thought Process

- The naive nested loop recomputes `k-1` of the same additions per step; the
  window exists to delete that redundancy.
- Seed `maxSum` with the first window, never with `0` — otherwise every negative
  array returns `0`, which is not a real window.
- The variable-size sibling (grow the right edge, shrink the left while a
  condition holds) solves "smallest subarray with sum ≥ target" and
  "longest substring without repeats"; recognising which of the two you need is
  most of the work.
